dossiers.name: The Allman Brothers Band
dossiers.summary: A group defined by two-guitar conversation, dual drummers, and a performance archive that spans distinct eras. Its lineups and live releases should be dated precisely rather than compressed into one timeless band.

facts.text: The original six assembled in Jacksonville, Florida, on March 26, 1969.
Duane and Dickey Betts played guitar; Gregg sang and played organ; Berry Oakley played bass; Butch Trucks and Jaimoe handled drums.
The band’s self-titled debut album appeared in November 1969.
Idlewild South followed in September 1970.
The breakthrough At Fillmore East was recorded during the March 1971 Fillmore engagement and released in July.
Duane Allman died on October 29, 1971, shortly after the original Fillmore release.
The band’s later history included Warren Haynes, Allen Woody, Oteil Burbridge and Derek Trucks joining in different periods.
The October 28 Beacon Theatre concert is documented as the band’s final performance.

open_questions: Complete verified personnel timelines for every lineup.
Separate release dates, performance dates, and master-tape sources for the same concert.

dossiers.name: Grateful Dead
dossiers.summary: The Dead’s performance history is best explored through individual nights and tape lineages, not through a simple list of famous dates. Official show records and label releases establish different kinds of evidence.

facts.text: The musicians played as the Warlocks in 1965 before adopting the Grateful Dead name later that year.
Early members included Jerry Garcia, Bob Weir, Ron McKernan, Bill Kreutzmann and Phil Lesh.
The band became associated with Ken Kesey’s Acid Tests by December 1965.
Official show records document the Boston, Cornell and Buffalo concerts on three consecutive May nights.
The Cornell concert includes Scarlet Begonias and Fire on the Mountain, followed later by Morning Dew.
Rhino issued Cornell 5/8/77 officially as part of a larger four-show May 1977 archival program.

open_questions: Associate audience, soundboard and matrix recordings with distinct lineage evidence.
Document individual performance transitions without equating title adjacency with segues.

dossiers.name: Phish
dossiers.angle: 1983 onward · The setlist as a map
dossiers.summary: Phish’s own concert archive and LivePhish releases make it possible to distinguish performed material, archival recordings, and fan annotations. Performance-specific notes matter more than generalized claims about legendary jams.

facts.text: Phish began around the University of Vermont in 1983 after Trey Anastasio sought fellow musicians.
Jon Fishman, Mike Gordon and Jeff Holdsworth were among the early participants.
Keyboardist Page McConnell joined in 1985; Holdsworth departed soon afterward.
Phish performed a three-set New Year’s Eve concert at Madison Square Garden on December 31, 1995.
The 1995 New Year’s Eve album credits Paul Languedoc as recording engineer.
The August 22 Magnaball event included three conventional sets and a separate Drive-In Jam.
The Phish.net entry documents transitions and an additional Mind Left Body Jam within Cities.

open_questions: Distinguish official setlists from fan-described teases and jam labels.
Build performance-specific song relationships rather than assuming all versions are alike.

dossiers.name: Goose
dossiers.angle: Modern improvisation · Current roster is time-sensitive
dossiers.summary: Goose illustrates why contemporary band profiles require a dated editorial snapshot. The band’s own biography establishes its current public roster and direct pathways to authorized live-music services.

facts.text: The official biography lists Rick Mitarotonda on guitar and vocals.
Peter Anspach is listed on vocals, keyboards and guitar.
Trevor Weekz is listed on bass, and Cotter Ellis on drums.
The band says it recorded its debut Moon Cabin in a New Hampshire barn in 2016.
The official site links fans to live recordings on Bandcamp and nugs.net.
The band’s official homepage identifies BIG MODERN! as its featured new studio album.

open_questions: Create first-party dated tour-announcement records, with publication and modification timestamps.
Document show-specific sit-ins from authorized concert descriptions.

dossiers.name: Oysterhead
dossiers.angle: A collaboration with a traceable origin
dossiers.summary: Oysterhead offers an unusually clear link between the Phish and Primus/Police worlds, documented by the participating guitarist’s project archive.

facts.text: Oysterhead began as a festival-period superjam at New Orleans’ Saenger Theatre.
The trio consisted of Trey Anastasio, Les Claypool and Stewart Copeland.
The musicians reconvened at the Barn in April 2001 to record The Grand Pecking Order.
The Grand Pecking Order has thirteen indexed tracks on Trey Anastasio’s official album page.
Trey’s project archive documents two February 2020 reunion concerts in Broomfield, Colorado.

open_questions: Add the two 2020 nights as separate verified concert records.
Document song-by-song author and guest credits without inferring them from band membership.

dossiers.name: Duane Allman
dossiers.summary: Duane Allman’s documented studio collaborations and short touring career are critical to connecting blues, soul, and live improvisation histories.

facts.text: Duane brought together the musicians who became the original Allman Brothers Band in Jacksonville.
The band’s official biography characterizes Duane’s interplay with Dickey Betts as twin-guitar dialogue.
Duane participated in Derek and the Dominos’ Layla and Other Assorted Love Songs sessions.
Duane played in the Fillmore East concerts subsequently documented by the expanded box set.
The official release notes describe the Painters Mill performance as Duane’s final concert.
Duane died after a motorcycle accident in Macon, Georgia, at age 24.

open_questions: Build sessionography with source-specific personnel credits.
Keep live performance claims separate from commercial release metadata.

dossiers.name: Trey Anastasio
dossiers.summary: Trey’s official project history provides a source-backed bridge between bands without implying every collaboration was a concert sit-in.

facts.text: Trey Anastasio is a founding member of Phish.
Trey performed with Les Claypool and Stewart Copeland in the original Oysterhead superjam.
Trey was part of Oysterhead’s Grand Pecking Order recording project.
His co-written score for Hands on a Hardbody received a Tony nomination.
Trey joined surviving Grateful Dead members for five fiftieth-anniversary stadium concerts.
Phish’s Baker’s Dozen residency at Madison Square Garden lasted thirteen nights.

open_questions: Attach precise show dates and personnel to each guest appearance.
Do not infer that a documented joint project means every member has shared other stages.

dossiers.name: Derek Trucks
dossiers.summary: Derek Trucks is a particularly valuable bridge for musician genealogy because his career crosses generations of the Allman Brothers Band.

facts.text: In an archived interview, Derek recalled sitting in with the Allman Brothers as a preteen.
Derek joined the Allman Brothers Band in 1999.
He described the 1999 frontline as Derek Trucks, Oteil Burbridge and Dickey Betts.
Derek described Jimmy Herring joining the guitar lineup during a transitional period.
Derek’s interview describes playing alongside Warren Haynes after Haynes returned.

open_questions: Document individual Allmans lineups by show date.
Add original sourced Tedeschi Trucks Band chronology before making additional crossover claims.

dossiers.name: Warren Haynes
dossiers.summary: Warren’s career is a useful test of time-aware network links: band membership changed, and a simple graph edge hides the sequence.

facts.text: An archived account places Warren in Dickey Betts’ band before the Allman Brothers reunion.
He joined the Allman Brothers Band for their 1989 reunion.
His playing and compositions contributed to the band’s early-1990s recordings.
Warren and bassist Allen Woody departed to concentrate on Gov’t Mule.
Archived interviews document Warren returning to the Allmans after Dickey Betts left.

open_questions: Resolve return dates with first-party lineup ledgers before publishing year-level membership intervals.
Keep historical ensemble membership separate from current roster assumptions.

dossiers.name: Rick Mitarotonda
dossiers.summary: Rick Mitarotonda’s public profile currently has verified core-role information, but our archive does not yet have enough corroborated session history or concert-specific appearances for a detailed personal discography.

facts.text: Goose identifies Rick Mitarotonda as one of its four current members.
The band identifies him as a vocalist and guitarist.
Goose traces its recording history to the 2016 debut Moon Cabin.
The official Goose website provides links to its Bandcamp and nugs live catalogs.

open_questions: Validate individual songwriting credits against album credits.
Add sourced guest appearances and the first dated authorized recording references.

dossiers.name: Allmans · Fillmore East, March 12 early
dossiers.summary: The expanded 2014 box set distinguishes this opening March 12 performance from the second show that night. They must never be collapsed into a single recording.

facts.text: Disc 1 of the expanded 2014 Fillmore collection documents the first March 12 performance.
The disc includes Statesboro Blues, Trouble No More and In Memory of Elizabeth Reed.
The same disc also includes an extended You Don’t Love Me.
The six-disc edition was issued in 2014 and distinguishes four March performances.

open_questions: Index the missing Disc 1 recording reference in the canonical source ledger.

dossiers.name: Allmans · Fillmore East, March 12 late
dossiers.summary: The second March 12 performance was separately documented on Disc 2 of the later archival edition, including material not on the corresponding first-show disc.

facts.text: Disc 2 of the six-disc Fillmore set covers the second March 12 performance.
The recorded program includes Whipping Post and Hot ’Lanta.
In Memory of Elizabeth Reed and You Don’t Love Me are also separately documented for this set.
The archival release presents this set individually rather than as one undifferentiated March 12 concert.

open_questions: Review whether the original 1971 album combines recordings from different March 12–13 sets.

dossiers.name: Allmans · Fillmore East, March 13 late
dossiers.summary: The second March 13 concert occupies parts of two discs in the expanded archival release. Its treatment illustrates why one show may correspond to multiple release tracks or discs.

facts.text: Disc 4 carries the first part of the March 13 second show.
Disc 5 continues that same second show.
The documented performance includes Mountain Jam.
The released sequence includes Drunken Hearted Boy with Elvin Bishop.

open_questions: Represent multi-disc release segments without inventing separate concert entities.

dossiers.name: Allmans · Fillmore East closing night
dossiers.summary: Official show records and later box-set releases document the performance from the venue’s closing weekend. The date is not one of the original March recording nights.

facts.text: The official concert archive lists the band at Fillmore East on June 27, 1971.
The documented set includes Midnight Rider, Whipping Post and You Don’t Love Me.
Disc 6 of The 1971 Fillmore East Recordings is dedicated to this closing show.
The deluxe Eat a Peach release also includes the June 27 concert.

open_questions: Compare differing mixes and edit points across the deluxe edition and six-disc box.

dossiers.name: Allmans · Atlanta Pop Festival second appearance
dossiers.summary: This show exposes a classic archival pitfall: the marketed date and the actual clock date differ. The original release liner notes are unusually explicit about the discrepancy.

facts.text: The official release labels the second festival recording July 5.
The release notes say the second performance began at 3:50 a.m. on July 6.
Johnny Winter appears on the issued Mountain Jam from the second festival performance.
The festival’s two performances were issued together commercially in 2003.

open_questions: Retain billed and clock dates as separate typed fields rather than overwriting the original show date.

dossiers.name: Allmans · Ludlow Garage
dossiers.summary: The band’s concert archive and the commercial release point to related music, but the recording date has competing documentary labels. Both should remain visible.

facts.text: The official show database lists an April 4 concert at Ludlow Garage in Cincinnati.
The event entry notes a receipts ledger documenting two nights at the venue.
An archival comment notes that a release booklet gave April 11 instead.
The official discography displays a 1990 release field while the descriptive text says released in 1991.
The commercial edition includes a forty-four-minute Mountain Jam.

open_questions: Seek original tape box or contemporary documentation before resolving performance date conclusively.

dossiers.name: Allmans · Painters Mill, October 17
dossiers.summary: The official archival release describes both the significance and limitations of this audience tape, including its unusual origin.

facts.text: The group’s official release identifies the Painters Mill concert as Duane Allman’s last show.
Sam Idas recorded the performance on a handheld cassette machine.
The tape was a spontaneous audience capture, not a purpose-built multitrack concert recording.
The Final Note issued eight documented songs from the performance in 2020.

open_questions: Document which songs are absent from the surviving cassette before claiming a complete setlist.

dossiers.name: Grateful Dead · Cornell
dossiers.summary: Cornell is a prime example of three separate archival objects: the original concert, circulating recorded sources, and later official commercial release.

facts.text: The official Dead show archive lists the concert at Cornell’s Barton Hall.
The published set includes Scarlet Begonias, Fire on the Mountain and Morning Dew.
Rhino officially released Cornell 5/8/77 after the Betty Board master tapes had been acquired.
Cornell was issued individually and in the four-show Get Shown the Light box.
Rhino credits Betty Cantor-Jackson soundboard masters, Plangent Processes transfers and Jeffrey Norman mastering for the four-show set.

open_questions: Crosswalk the audience, soundboard, matrix and official release sources without declaring them interchangeable.

dossiers.name: Grateful Dead · Buffalo
dossiers.summary: The night after Cornell has its own canonical show, setlist, and performance sequence—valuable context for exploring how recurring songs changed.

facts.text: The official show archive identifies War Memorial Auditorium in Buffalo.
The set begins with Help on the Way, Slipknot! and Franklin’s Tower in sequence.
The second half includes Estimated Prophet, The Other One and Comes a Time.
Buffalo is one of the four concert dates packaged in Get Shown the Light.

open_questions: Compare distinct transitions with Cornell only after reviewing recordings, not merely adjacent song titles.

dossiers.name: Phish · Madison Square Garden NYE
dossiers.summary: This show offers exceptionally strong dual-source documentation: a first-party concert setlist and the later official release credits.

facts.text: The official archive describes a three-set performance with encore.
The third set includes Auld Lang Syne, Weekapaug Groove and You Enjoy Myself.
The release credits Paul Languedoc for the original concert recording.
The official concert entry documents the subsequent complete-concert audio edition.
The show record notes Runaway Jim featured Trey on an additional percussion kit during the jam.

open_questions: Avoid translating track timings into jam-analysis claims without close listening and attribution.

dossiers.name: Phish · Magnaball
dossiers.summary: Official setlist and community annotations supply different levels of detail. The extra Drive-In Jam deserves its own context without pretending it was a conventional fourth set.

facts.text: Phish performed at Watkins Glen International during Magnaball.
The official listing divides the main performance into three sets and an encore.
The official site separately lists the Drive-In Jam after the main program.
Phish.net identifies an intervening Mind Left Body Jam in the third-set Cities sequence.
Phish.net describes the Drive-In Jam being performed behind a projection screen.

open_questions: Separate official setlist data from interpretive descriptions and tease annotations.

dossiers.name: Allmans · The final Beacon concert
dossiers.summary: The official database preserves multiple set segments and a commercial recording reference from the band’s final public concert.

facts.text: The official archive identifies this as the band’s Beacon Theatre concert in New York.
The setlist includes Little Martha, Blue Sky, Whipping Post and Trouble No More.
The archive links Final Concert 10-28-14 as a later official archival release.
The archive separates multiple sets, rather than a single continuous song list.

open_questions: Distinguish the archived concert from the 2024 commercial release.
